qualification: Literal original-table schemas and source constructor outputs. The source time metadata is a JSON YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS string; its assessment qualifies native software-timer admission >=1526969436 but no maximum calendar year or clock integer width/wrap. Zero serial/cache and epoch clock are explicit synthetic policy, not native boot observations

aes.outbound_padding: PKCS7 including a full block at exact capacity
aes.inbound_safe_policy: require and remove PKCS7; native does not validate it

base64.safe_policy: strict alphabet and complete AES blocks

primitive_contract.selector: request int32 ==0 selects device key; all nonzero values select generic key; replies use boolean1 for scan/bind,0 for cache/timers
primitive_contract.uid: int32 echoed; no uint8 session mask

deviations: Strict atomic parser rejects bool, null, string and float scalar writes rather than native cJSON valueint coercion or faults
At most34 names avoids the original exact35 empty-output/overflow path; status stops at the first empty or at-least16-byte name, while commands retain long source names
Known scalar cache stores requested int32, not its UART bitmask width; no invented immediate mainboard ACK or calibrated readout
Synthetic clock starts1970 UTC and advances monotonically; software timers use in-memory persistence and an explicit daily/weekly synthetic scheduler
The synthetic datetime clock saturates at 9999-12-31 23:59:59 and stops scheduler day stepping after that final date; this is bounded safety policy, not source wrap behavior
W06 unassociated selector0/1 and JoyLink fan have literal schemas but no invented emitted MID/profile
Strict target and crypto checks replace unsafe native unchecked field access and unvalidated inbound padding
